identity.title: TTSDS2: Resources and Benchmark for Evaluating Human-Quality Text to Speech Systems

problem.claim: Evaluating text-to-speech systems, especially systems producing speech close to real speech, is challenging and resource-intensive.

gap.claim: MOS scores are difficult to compare across studies, while objective metrics are rarely validated against subjective measures and both metric types face challenges on recent TTS systems.

contributions.claim: Introduces TTSDS2, described as a more robust and improved version of TTSDS.
Releases over 11,000 subjective opinion-score ratings, a pipeline for recreating a multilingual test dataset to reduce data leakage, and a 14-language TTS benchmark.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish TTSDS2 as a more robust and improved successor to TTSDS.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TTSDS2 was the only one of 16 compared metrics with Spearman correlation above 0.50 for every evaluated domain and subjective score, across multiple domains and languages.
The authors report releasing evaluation resources spanning subjective ratings, leakage-avoidance test-data reconstruction, and multilingual benchmarking.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies evaluation cost and difficulty, limited comparability of MOS, weak objective-metric validation, and challenges posed by near-real synthetic speech.
The work introduces TTSDS2 as an improved and more robust TTSDS variant.
Across domains and languages, the authors report TTSDS2 uniquely exceeding 0.50 Spearman correlation for every evaluated domain and subjective score among 16 metrics.
The authors additionally release ratings, a multilingual data-recreation pipeline, and a 14-language benchmark.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a metric proposal with a quantified comparison against 16 metrics and specifies the correlation threshold, domains, languages, and subjective-score coverage.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes the claimed distinction and evaluation scope easier to inspect from a compact abstract.
lessons.application: When presenting a new evaluation metric, state the comparator set, metric, threshold, and coverage conditions alongside the proposal.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no meaningful comparator set or agreed evaluation target exists.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the compared metrics, datasets, rating protocols, sample sizes by domain or language, or statistical uncertainty.
It does not provide details needed to assess how the data-leakage pipeline works or how the benchmark is constructed.
